text: At one twenty-three and forty seconds, the button marked A Z five was pressed. Every control rod began to drive in. But the rods had a fatal design flaw. Below the boron, each one carried a long section of graphite. It was there to make the rods more effective, by keeping water out of the channel when a rod was pulled out. But with the rods pulled almost all the way out, the first thing to slide into the bottom of the core was that graphite, pushing the water out. So for the first few seconds, the shutdown button added power at the bottom of the reactor, instead of taking it away. And the rods were slow. Around eighteen seconds to go all the way in.
